test_title: RRB ALP CBT-II (Heat Engine) Official Paper (Held On: 02 May, 2025 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: When using a multimeter to measure current, which of the following is correct?

options.text: The multimeter is connected directly to the power source.
The multimeter is connected only across resistive components.
The multimeter is connected in parallel with the load.
The multimeter is connected in series with the load.

solution:
The correct answer is __The multimeter is connected in series with the load**(Option 4)**.__

**__Key Points__**

__
 
• When measuring current, the multimeter must be connected in series__ with the circuit.
 
• This is because current flows through the multimeter to measure the amount passing through the circuit.
 
• Connecting the multimeter in parallel can damage the device or result in incorrect readings.
 
• Always ensure the multimeter is set to the correct current measurement range before connecting.
 
• Use appropriate probes and maintain proper polarity to ensure accurate measurements and safety.

**__Additional Information__**

 
• **Common Multimeter Mistakes:**

 
 
• Connecting the multimeter in parallel while measuring current can cause short circuits.
 
• Using incorrect settings or ranges may lead to device damage or erroneous results.
 
 
 
• **Precautions While Using Multimeters:**
 
 
• Ensure the probes are in the correct ports for current measurement (e.g., COM and mA/A).
 
• Do not exceed the maximum current rating of the multimeter.
